EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East faces a critical escalation as the United States formally renewed military operations against Iran and declared the reinstatement of a naval blockade on Iranian shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, effective July 14. President Trump stated the US would act as the "Guardian of the Hormuz Strait," imposing a 20% transit fee on all commercial cargo, while Iran defiantly rejected US interference, calling it an act of war and responding with claims of damaging US military bases in regional allies.

IRAN
US forces continued offensive strikes against Iran, with CENTCOM reporting dozens of precise attacks on July 13 targeting air defense systems, coastal radar sites, missile and drone capabilities, and small boats. For the first time, US sea drones (Corsair unmanned surface vessels) were reportedly used to strike a submarine and ship maintenance facility in Bandar Abbas. Iranian state media and channels reported numerous explosions across southern Iran, including Bandar Abbas, Chabahar, Qeshm, Bushehr, Sirik, Jask, Khondab, Mahshahr, Behbahan, Andimeshk, Dezful, Ahvaz, Abadan, and Khorramshahr. One person was killed and four injured in a US strike on a water pumping station in Mahshahr, and three "fighters" (Iraj Sardarpoor, Asghar Sardarpoor, Ali Tajbakhsh) were reported killed in an airstrike in Abadan. Power outages were reported in parts of Khuzestan province, including Ahvaz, Dezful, and Behbahan, potentially linked to the strikes.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed retaliatory attacks, stating its Aerospace Force destroyed a US base in Bahrain (Sheikh Isa Air Base, targeting helicopter maintenance, P-8 electronic warfare aircraft hangar, and drone command/control center) and US bases in Kuwait (Ali Al Salem Air Base, destroying fuel depots and a Patriot air defense system; Ahmad Al Jaber Air Base, hitting a strategic FPS radar system). The IRGC also claimed to have targeted a radar facility in Oman and successfully shot down two US LUCAS drones over Bandar Abbas and Lar. Iran's central military command, Khatam al-Anbiya, warned that any US interference in Hormuz management or logistical support from regional countries would be considered an act of war.

Economically, global oil prices (Brent crude) surged by approximately 5% to over $81-83 per barrel amid the heightened tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s Foreign Minister Araghchi affirmed Iran's role as the "Guardian of the Strait" and sarcastically commented on Trump's proposed 20% fee, suggesting Iran would be "fairer." Iranian President پزشکیان met with the Russian Energy Minister, emphasizing cooperation against unilateralism.

ISRAEL
Domestically, the "Torah Study Law" passed its second and third readings in the Knesset with a vote of 63-52, drawing fierce condemnation from opposition leaders (Lapid, Bennett, Eisenkot, Liberman, Golan, Tropper) and former Defense Minister Gantz, who described it as an "anti-Zionist" act damaging to the IDF during wartime. The IDF Chief of Staff reportedly warned that the law would provide a "negative incentive" for enlistment and harm military cohesion. Internal Likud politics saw Prime Minister Netanyahu secure 7-8 reserved spots on the party list. The security cabinet is scheduled to meet on July 14 at 20:00.

Militarily, the IDF announced it killed Mustafa Owaisi, a Palestinian weapons smuggler, in an airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip on July 12, accusing him of attempting to rebuild Hamas's military wing in violation of the ceasefire agreement. The IDF also reported conducting airstrikes deep inside Lebanon, with residents in the Western Galilee reporting strong explosions.

On the home front, two grenade explosions, deemed criminal, occurred in South Tel Aviv, lightly injuring one person. An 80-year-old woman drowned in מכמורת, and a 14-year-old boy was critically injured in a fall from a horse near Lakia. An emergency drill involving substantial security forces is planned for Jerusalem on July 14.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF conducted an airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip, killing Mustafa Owaisi, described as a Hamas weapons smuggler attempting to rebuild the group's naval and aerial capabilities, which the IDF stated was a violation of the ceasefire agreement. Palestinian reports indicated Israeli airstrikes in Rafah and Khan Younis. COGAT reported that Hamas forcibly took over a UN food distribution center in Jabalia, attacking aid truck drivers and disrupting aid delivery for thousands of families.

LEBANON
The IDF reported conducting airstrikes "deep into Lebanon," with strong explosions heard by residents in the Western Galilee. Israeli forces were also reported to have demolished residential buildings in the southern Lebanese town of Kafr Tebnit after residents were displaced. The Givati brigade reportedly completed five months of intensive operational activity across the border in Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Syrian Parliament reportedly convened for the first time since the fall of the Assad regime (an event from outside the 24-hour window, but mentioned in feed). Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zeidi arrived in Washington for official talks. No other specific militia activity or airstrikes within Syria or Iraq were reported in the last 24 hours.

GULF STATES
The region witnessed heightened tensions with direct attacks and counter-attacks. Saudi Arabia conducted airstrikes on Sana'a International Airport in Yemen, which the Yemeni government confirmed was to prevent an Iranian Mahan Air plane (carrying Houthi officials) from landing. In retaliation, Houthi forces launched six ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport, forcing flight suspensions and passenger evacuations. Saudi air defenses claimed to have intercepted these threats. Reports of further explosions in Jeddah and the Aseer region of Saudi Arabia were also noted.
Kuwait's military reported dealing with "hostile aerial targets" in its airspace, coinciding with Iranian claims of destroying US bases there. Bahrain experienced multiple alarm activations, and the IRGC claimed to have destroyed a US base on Sheikh Isa island. The UAE's DP World announced plans for a new port in Fujairah to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, signaling concern over regional security.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Reinstates Naval Blockade on Iran:** President Trump announced the US would reinstate a naval blockade on Iranian shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, effective July 14, 23:00 Iran time (8 PM GMT), stating the US would act as the "Guardian of the Hormuz Strait" and levy a 20% fee on all cargo.
2.  **Expanded US Strikes on Iran:** CENTCOM confirmed dozens of precision strikes on July 13 against Iranian air defense systems, coastal radar, missile/drone sites, and small boats. For the first time, US "Corsair" sea drones were reportedly used to target a submarine and ship maintenance facility in Bandar Abbas.
3.  **Iranian Retaliatory Strikes on US Bases:** Iran's IRGC claimed to have destroyed US military assets at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain and Ali Al Salem and Ahmad Al Jaber Air Bases in Kuwait, and hit a radar facility in Oman, in response to US aggression.
4.  **UK Designates IRGC as Terrorist Organization:** The British government officially proscribed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization, making membership or support a criminal offense.
5.  **Escalation in Yemen-Saudi Conflict:** Saudi Arabia struck Sana'a International Airport to prevent an Iranian Mahan Air flight carrying a Houthi delegation from landing. In retaliation, Houthis launched six ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport, resulting in flight suspensions and passenger evacuations.
6.  **Ahmadinejad Detained for Alleged Mossad Ties:** The New York Times reported that former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is under house arrest by IRGC intelligence, accused of long-standing ties with Israeli Mossad, who allegedly cultivated him as a potential post-regime leader.
7.  **"Torah Study Law" Passed in Israel:** The Israeli Knesset approved the controversial "Torah Study Law" by a vote of 63-52, drawing strong condemnation from opposition parties and the IDF Chief of Staff for potentially harming military morale during wartime.
8.  **Oil Price Surge:** Global oil prices, including Brent crude, increased by approximately 5% to over $81-83 per barrel, driven by escalating tensions and threats to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
9.  **Hormuz Bypass Initiative:** DP World announced plans for a new multipurpose port and container terminal in Fujairah, UAE, aimed at reducing reliance on Dubai's Jebel Ali hub and bypassing the Strait of Hormuz amid rising security concerns.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of a wider regional conflict is critically high, driven by direct US-Iran military confrontations and escalatory actions in the Strait of Hormuz. The US reinstatement of a naval blockade and declaration of "Guardianship" over Hormuz, coupled with a 20% transit fee, represents a significant challenge to Iranian sovereignty claims and is explicitly rejected by Tehran as an act of war. Iranian retaliatory strikes on US bases in Gulf states and threats to expand conflict to any cooperating countries mark a serious escalation. The Houthi threat to close the Bab al-Mandeb and Hormuz straits in response to Saudi aggression further risks international shipping and could trigger broader military intervention. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, US military installations in Gulf states (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman), and the Saudi-Yemen border. Both sides have articulated red lines, with Iran warning that any US interference in Hormuz or support from regional allies will lead to the "flames of war" engulfing the entire region.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States**, through President Trump, formally notified Congress of renewed combat operations against Iran, announced the reinstatement of a naval blockade on Iranian shipping, and declared the US as the "Guardian of the Hormuz Strait," imposing a 20% fee on all cargo. Secretary of State Marco Rubio initiated a campaign to "dismantle the threat" posed by the International Criminal Court to US sovereignty.
The **United Kingdom** officially proscribed the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization, banning support for the force.
The **UN's International Maritime Organization (IMO)** stated its opposition to mandatory fees for transit through international straits, pending further details from Trump's statement. UN Secretary-General Guterres called for a full ceasefire in the Gulf region.
**Russia's** President Putin warned of a powerful and multi-fold response to any attack on Russian territory. Its Energy Minister met with the Iranian President, affirming scientific, industrial, and economic cooperation against "unilateralism."
**Qatar** called for dialogue, diplomacy, and de-escalation to prevent further consequences of the ongoing attacks.
**Oman** is continuing political and technical talks with Iran regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz.
**Yemen's Sana'a-based government (Houthis)** condemned Saudi Arabia's attack on Sana'a Airport as a breach of international law and a direct violation of humanitarian law, declaring the end of the de-escalation phase and a "new phase of war."

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several claims in the intelligence feed remain unverified or contradictory. President Trump's assertion that "Khamenei is dead, his son 90% dead" lacks any corroborating evidence and contradicts reports of the Supreme Leader's funeral on July 6. The extent and veracity of Iran's claims regarding the destruction of US bases and military assets in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman require independent confirmation, especially given CENTCOM's denial of any US casualties in Kuwait. Reports of explosions in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and at the Ben Zayed base in the UAE are similarly unconfirmed by official sources. The specific causes and exact locations of power outages across Iranian provinces like Khuzestan are not definitively linked solely to US strikes, though timing suggests a connection. The reported GPS disruptions in Tehran also lack verification regarding their cause or extent. Propaganda indicators are evident in both Iranian and Houthi messaging, emphasizing defiance, condemning adversaries, and selectively reporting successes or threats. Reporting gaps exist concerning detailed battle damage assessments from either side, the exact operational impact of the "Torah Study Law" on the IDF, and the full scope of the UK's IRGC proscription.
